technical_and_design_decisions: Implement optional queue/topic cleanup (U1) on the container side using Spring AMQP's RabbitAdmin and RabbitManagementTemplate (or direct REST API), triggered by an optional '--clean' flag on the stream destroy command.
For error notifications (U2), leverage Spring Integration error channels; create a per-stream/module error channel and expose failures via a dedicated REST endpoint or message bus.
For security (U3), use Spring Security with Spring Boot auto-configuration to secure REST endpoints; configure via properties and support shell/UI authentication.

For HTTP module (U5), build a new Spring Boot MVC module with embedded Tomcat, reusing Spring MVC controllers for richer content-type negotiation and full header mapping instead of rewriting in existing HTTP source.
For status notifications (U6), implement a common client-side polling strategy and augment with server-side event propagation over the existing message bus (e.g., Rabbit) to notify UI clients.
For SFTP source (U7), use Spring Integration SFTP inbound adapter; use an embedded SFTP server (Apache Mina) for testing.
For ElasticSearch sink (U8), use Spring Data Elasticsearch (or official client) to index data in real-time with batching.
assumptions: The increment targets the Spring XD codebase; existing build, CI, and test infrastructure are available and reusable.

technical_and_design_decisions: All new code will be written in Go, consistent with the existing Hyperledger Fabric codebase.
Solo ordering service will be implemented as a pluggable orderer type using gRPC Broadcast/Deliver services, with an in-memory ledger (slice/map) and block indexing to support seek and reconnection.
Friendly chaincode names and deployment policies will be stored as additional metadata in the Lifecycle System Chaincode (LSCC) world state, keyed by chaincode ID.
State cache will be implemented as a local in-memory read cache inside the peer's transaction simulator, populated on read and invalidated upon block commit.
The CLI will be extracted into a separate Go module that interacts with peers and orderers via gRPC, eliminating the link dependency on RocksDB and other peer internal packages.
Documentation will be authored in Markdown and published to the Hyperledger documentation site / GitHub Pages with a central index linked from hyperledger.org.
GitHub mirror will be achieved by configuring Gerrit replication to a public GitHub repository; no new application code required beyond configuration.
assumptions: The developer is familiar with the existing Fabric architecture, Go, and the relevant toolchains.
Existing CI, build, and test infrastructure can be extended with minor configuration for new modules and binaries.
Solo orderer does not require persistent storage or crash recovery, as per the specification.
Existing signature/endorsement policy formats are sufficient for deployment policies; no new policy language is needed.
State cache consistency is maintained by invalidating entries on commit; no distributed caching is required.
Documentation tasks are limited to upgrade flow authoring and indexing; they do not include a full documentation rewrite.
CLI binaries for Mac and Windows are provided as cross-compiled executables without graphical installers.
Effort includes unit and basic integration testing but excludes extensive performance tuning, security audits, and production deployment.

technical_and_design_decisions: Use existing Mule module/connector architecture for new WebSocket and JDBC components.
NIO stack activation controlled by a new boolean property in deploy.properties, read at startup to select transport layer.
WebSocket components implemented as standard Mule message source/processor using Java WebSocket/NIO APIs.
Registry features (pairing, endpoint management, dynamic resolution, throttling) integrated via an assumed RESTful JSON API client.
Dynamic router implemented as a router message processor that queries the Registry for endpoint resolution at runtime.
Throttling policies enforced by a flow interceptor/message processor using a token-bucket algorithm, configured from Registry.
Business events and transaction IDs exposed through SLF4J MDC and logged at DEBUG/INFO level during development.
MVEL dependency upgraded to 2.1.8 with minimal compatibility wrappers for DataMapper and expression evaluation.
JDBC connectivity for Oracle, PostgreSQL, Sybase, MS SQL Server, DB2 provided as pre-configured datasource templates on top of existing Mule JDBC connector.
JDBC query logging implemented via statement wrapper that logs SQL at DEBUG level when enabled.
assumptions: Detailed specifications on the referenced internal wiki pages are unavailable; functionality is inferred from the user story descriptions.
The Registry exposes REST APIs for account pairing, endpoint management, dynamic endpoint resolution, and throttling policy application.
Database JDBC drivers are available in the runtime/classpath; only configuration templates and defaults are delivered.
The developer is experienced with the Mule codebase and has a working build environment; no environment setup effort is included.
Effort covers design, implementation, and automated testing by the same developer, excluding separate manual QA, user training, and production deployment.
MySQL JDBC support is already present and requires no additional work.
